# Requirements Consistency Checklist: Bug triage run ships its own work

**Purpose**: Validate the specification's requirements for completeness, clarity and internal consistency, concentrating on supersession, branch coverage, destructive-action guards, and testability
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Supersession Is Stated, Not Implied

- [ ] CHK001 Is every superseded requirement identified by its own identifier rather than described only by what it forbade? [Traceability, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the supersession itself written as a normative requirement rather than as narrative commentary in an assumptions or notes section? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the spec state where the supersession must be recorded, so that a reader of the superseded document can discover it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it explicitly required that the superseded record not be rewritten to appear as though it always said the new thing? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements that deliberately restate an existing prohibition distinguished from those that supersede one, so a reader cannot mistake a restatement for a change? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the boundary of the supersession bounded — does the spec say which earlier requirements are untouched, not only which are replaced? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the requirements governing the published record of distributed components specific about what "accurate" means for them? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK008 Does the spec require stale pointers to superseded records to be found, or only that known ones be corrected? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-035]

## Every Branch Has a Defined Outcome

- [ ] CHK009 For each choice the run offers, is the outcome of every option specified rather than only the expected one? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-021, §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the requirements explicit that a choice which cannot be carried out is withheld rather than offered and then refused? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK011 Is stating the reason for a withheld choice required, rather than allowing the option to be silently absent? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the conditions that cause each choice to be withheld enumerated, or left to be inferred at implementation time? [Gap, Spec §FR-024, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the outcome defined for the case where a stage is skipped entirely, including what the shipping steps do with no change to carry? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the outcome defined for the case where a step's delegated work returns without having done what was asked? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the requirements clear about what happens to the workspace question when no review request was produced? [Coverage, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the run's behaviour specified for a remote at a forge no workflow supports, distinctly from having no remote at all? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the spec define the ordering constraint between committing and raising a review request as a requirement rather than an implied sequence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the requirements for the reassessment loop clear about what the re-entered stage receives, not only that it is re-entered? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the reporting obligation for a repeated cycle specified in a way that distinguishes it from reporting ordinary progress? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-011b]

## Destructive Actions Are Guarded

- [ ] CHK020 Is the precondition for discarding a line of work stated as a requirement, not left to the underlying tooling's own refusal? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the precondition for discarding a workspace stated separately from the one for discarding a line of work, given they guard different things? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec make clear that a workspace guard covers uncommitted work of any origin, not only work this run produced? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK023 Is it required that no blanket or earlier approval can be read as authorising a destructive choice? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the scope of that approval ceiling defined — which approvals it covers and which it does not? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK025 Are the requirements explicit that a workspace the run did not create is never offered for disposal? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK026 Is confirming what actually happened to the workspace required, rather than trusting that the requested action succeeded? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the least-destructive option required to be the recommended one, with the reason stated as a requirement rather than a convention? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec address the case where the reports produced by the run exist only inside a workspace proposed for disposal? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-024]

## Requirements Are Independently Testable

- [ ] CHK029 Can each functional requirement be evaluated on its own, without depending on another requirement's interpretation? [Measurability]
- [ ] CHK030 Are requirements that use "MUST NOT" paired with an observable signal that would reveal a violation? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK031 Is "hand that job to the workflow that owns it" specified precisely enough that performing the work directly would be detectably non-compliant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK032 Is "facts rather than answers" defined well enough to distinguish a compliant handoff from a non-compliant one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK033 Are the requirements about recording the workspace arrangement specific about what must survive a loss of conversational context? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK034 Can each success criterion be verified without knowing how the feature is built? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001 to §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK035 Are the success criteria stated as absolutes ("100%", "no run") backed by requirements that make the absolute checkable? [Traceability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-003, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the verification obligation for the unchanged second forge's workflow specified concretely enough to be evidenced? [Measurability, Spec §FR-029a]
- [ ] CHK037 Are the sourcing and open-gap obligations for the written record measurable, rather than a matter of judgement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-032, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the single-location rule for durable working rules stated with enough precision to detect a duplicate? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033]

## Ambiguities, Conflicts and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK039 Do any two requirements in the shipping group impose orderings that cannot both hold? [Conflict, Spec §FR-012 to §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the assumption that the delegated workflows gate their own decisions stated, and are the consequences of it being false addressed? [Assumption]
- [ ] CHK041 Is the assumption that stage reports survive an interrupted run recorded and consistent with the requirements that read them? [Assumption, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK042 Are terms describing the workspace used consistently throughout, with no synonym introduced that could denote something different? [Consistency]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- This checklist was generated before `plan.md` existed, so every item is drawn from `spec.md` alone; no technical context informed it
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
